title: Cyrus and the Oath
premise: Sable Reyes has survived five years in the walled city of Verrin by hiding his gift for speaking with beasts behind a mask of harmless charm-seller. When the crown's new Inquisitor begins hunting the gifted, Sable is betrayed by a customer and dragged into the purge, only to discover that his gift is not random: he is the last living heir of the Oathkeepers, the order that once bound humans and beasts in covenant. Hunted across a winter that refuses to end, Sable must choose between the woman sworn to arrest him and the truth of his inheritance, reforge the broken covenant at the frozen Wellspring, and pay the Oath's price: a voice given up for every voice he wakes. He succeeds, at the cost of never speaking to beasts again in his own tongue, and returns to a city beginning, slowly, to unmake its laws.
about_author: Ansel Villalobos is the pen name of a former farrier from the high desert country who claims to have learned more about patience from horses than from any book. Cyrus and the Oath is their second novel and the first set in the world of Verrin.

chapters.title: Charms and Small Lies
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In the market of Verrin, Sable sells 'charms' that are really whispered bargains with pigeons and rats, keeping his gift hidden. A girl named Wren asks him to speak to her dying hound, and he refuses, afraid. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a gift that must stay buried.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Criers announce the Gift-Hunt: anyone with the old magic is to be surrendered or burned. Sable watches the crowd's fear turn hungry and realizes his five quiet years are over. Emotional beat: dread settling like the first snow.

chapters.title: The Hound That Spoke
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren returns at night with her dying hound, and Sable relents, easing its passing. The hound's last words name him 'Oathkeeper's blood.' Wren overhears everything. Emotional beat: tenderness curdling into danger.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Net
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Hale's POV. Hale, a former Oathkeeper's apprentice turned crown servant, works the city with cold efficiency, using Wren's report to build a case. He suspects Sable but wants proof. Emotional beat: the tragedy of a man who loved the old ways and now destroys them.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Market
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Wren, coerced by threats to her family, lures Sable into a trap. He escapes with help from a street-cat who owes him, but his shop burns and his identity is exposed. Emotional beat: betrayal, and the bitter knowledge that he'd have done the same.

chapters.title: Under the City
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The street-cat leads him through sewers to the Burrow, a hidden enclave of the last gifted. There he meets Maren, a beast-speaker elder who recognizes his bloodline. Emotional beat: cautious belonging after years alone.

chapters.title: The Broken Covenant
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren explains the history: the Oathkeepers bound human and beast realms in covenant at the Wellspring; the crown broke it a generation ago, and the endless winter is the realms' dying grief. Only Oathkeeper blood can reforge it. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: The Hunter's Doubt
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale interrogates Wren and sees his old mentor's teachings in the 'heresies' she describes. He begins to doubt the crown's story that the gifted caused the winter. Emotional beat: loyalty to duty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Raid on the Burrow
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Hale's soldiers find the Burrow. In the escape, Maren dies holding the tunnel open, charging Sable to reach the Wellspring before midwinter. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: The Road North
chapters.summary: Sable and Wren's alternating POV. Wren, fleeing her own betrayal, catches up to Sable and offers to guide him north through the passes she knows as a courier. Trust is grudging, tested, and slowly built. Emotional beat: two liars learning honesty.

chapters.title: What the Wolves Remember
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A wolf pack corners them on the pass; instead of fighting, Sable listens, and learns the beasts' side of the broken covenant: generations of abandoned promises. He swears, aloud, to answer them. Emotional beat: the first true act of Oathkeeping.

chapters.title: Hale at the Ford
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale corners the pair at a frozen river crossing. Wren takes a crossbow bolt meant for Sable; Hale, seeing her sacrifice, lets them go and burns his own warrant. Emotional beat: duty and conscience finally at war.

chapters.title: The Fevered Vigil
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Wren's wound turns to fever. Sable spends his gift's strength bargaining with carrion birds for medicine moss, weakening himself before the Wellspring. Emotional beat: love confessed to an unconscious listener.

chapters.title: The Crown's Winter Court
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale returns to face the crown, is condemned as a traitor, and escapes with evidence that the king's grandfather broke the covenant deliberately for power. Emotional beat: a loyal man becoming a rebel.

chapters.title: The Wellspring
chapters.summary: Sable and Wren's POV. They reach the frozen Wellspring and find it guarded by the Pale Stag, the covenant's first witness, who tests Sable with visions of every selfish thing he's done. Emotional beat: humility before inheritance.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: The Stag's POV (a rare beast-chapter). The Stag explains the Oath's terms: to reforge the covenant, an Oathkeeper must give up his own voice to the beasts forever — no more human speech, only theirs. Sable asks for a night to decide. Emotional beat: the true weight of the gift.

chapters.title: One Night of Words
chapters.summary: Sable and Wren's POV. Sable and Wren spend his last night of human speech talking — about his mother, her family, the life they won't have. They marry by firelight, unwitnessed but real. Emotional beat: love choosing its shape.

chapters.title: Hale's Last March
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale arrives at the Wellspring pursued by crown troops sent to seize the covenant's power for the throne. He chooses to stand with Sable against his former soldiers. Emotional beat: redemption bought with loyalty reversed.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Wellspring
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The troops attack as midwinter falls. Hale holds the pass at terrible cost; Wren fights beside Sable; the wolves of the pass answer Sable's earlier oath and turn the battle. Emotional beat: every debt of loyalty called in at once.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. At the heart of the Wellspring, Sable speaks the covenant's first words in a generation, then gives his voice as the price. The ice breaks; the winter begins to loosen; the realms breathe again. Emotional beat: sacrifice fulfilled, silence chosen freely.

chapters.title: The King's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Hale and Wren's POV. With the Stag as living witness and Hale's evidence, the crown's lie collapses; the Gift-Hunt is revoked and the old laws begin to fall. Hale takes up the ruined Oathkeeper order to rebuild it. Emotional beat: justice as slow repair, not triumph.

chapters.title: The Voice He Kept
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, epilogue. Spring comes to Verrin. Sable cannot speak human words, but Wren translates as he talks with the city's animals, and the market fills with open, unhidden magic. A young gifted child brings him a sparrow with a question. Emotional beat: an ending that is a beginning — inheritance passed on.
